bounded_statement: Within the visible files of this case only: each first-collection source item identified by k1 (u01 through u12) contributes exactly two rows, and the workflow enters both `a` measurements per item into scipy.stats.ttest_ind, a procedure that treats every entered value as an independent observation; the report's df=46.0 confirms all 48 values (24 per side) were entered without any per-unit aggregation.

counterevidence_considered.description: The k2 codes are all distinct across the 24 rows (v01–v24 each once), so the second entered sample contains no repeated units; the repetition is confined to the k1/a side. This limits but does not negate the finding, since one repeated side suffices to violate the procedure's independence assumption.

The task explicitly authorizes applying the procedure to the complete staged row sequence, so entry of all rows was directed rather than a workflow deviation; this is authorization for the entry, not evidence that the units are non-repeated.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

evidence.description: Task establishes k1 as the identifier of a first-collection source item measured by column a, so equal k1 codes denote the same unit.

evidence.description: The same k1 code u01 appears on two consecutive data rows, each contributing a distinct `a` value; the same twice-repeated pattern holds for every k1 code u01–u12 across lines 2–25.
evidence.observed_value: u01 appears in 2 rows (a=1.0 and a=1.5); 12 unique k1 codes over 24 rows

evidence.description: The workflow enters all per-row values into an independent-samples t-test with no per-unit aggregation or deduplication.
evidence.observed_value: st.ttest_ind applied to all 24 row values per column

evidence.description: The report's degrees of freedom equal 46, i.e. 24+24-2, confirming that every row-level value, including the repeated entries per k1 unit, was counted as an independent observation.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify by (a) checking whether equal k1 codes could denote distinct units — the task states k1 identifies a source item, leaving no reading under which two u01 rows are different first-collection items; (b) checking whether the workflow deduplicates or averages per k1 before testing — it maps every row's `a` directly into the test; (c) checking whether the report could reflect a deduplicated run — df=46.0 requires 48 entered values, matching all 24 rows per side, so no aggregation occurred. All falsification routes failed.

root_cause: The workflow reads every staged row and passes each row's `a` value directly into ttest_ind without collapsing repeated measurements of the same k1-identified source item into one entry per unit, so the same authorized independent unit is entered repeatedly into a row-independent procedure.
